title: Caller with old records is sent to Allen at the Tulane jazz archives
summary: A caller asks if Clyde McCoy is jazz and about her old records; Wiggs gives his view of the word jazz and praises Allen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: Well, I tell you, I hate to call anything jazz anymore, because everything south of Beethoven has been called jazz, and I don't know what jazz is and what jazz isn't. I know the kind of musicians that I like to play with, and they call that jazz, and that's the best I can do with that.
Uh-huh. Well, the reason I'm asking, I have a record, and it has a picture on it, like a painting on the record. Would that be worth anything? It's made by the Vogue Record Company.
It all depends on how old it is. Almost anything old is worth money.
Uh-huh. Well, what would you do to find out if it would be worth money? I have piles and piles of old jazz records.

Uh, you might... Dick Allen will be right over. I'd take it up to Mr. Allen at Tulane University. He's going to hit me in the head with something. Well, no, I'd be happy to... He knows more about jazz than anybody in America. That's a fact.
And I'm not saying that because he's next to me, but that's a fact, a cold fact.
Well, how do you get in touch with him other than...
He's up at the Tulane Library in the jazz archives. He's the head of the jazz archives. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. What's that big word, Dick? The curator of the jazz archives.
Well, I might get my record collection out and go check everything and bring them over to him. Well, I'll...
You can just make a list. You can... Yeah, if you make a list, he'll tell you what's what. But you can rely on anything he says.
